question.text: Regulation 91(D)(7) of LODR permits a Social Enterprise to:

answer.text: Suo moto confirm or deny any reported event or information to the SSE.
Delete any previously filed disclosure within 7 days without SSE approval.
Refuse to respond to SSE queries for up to 30 days.
Substitute a press release for a formal 91(D) filing.

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 91(D)(7) permits the SE to 'suo moto confirm or deny any reported event or information' to SSE. This supports the SE's ability to correct market rumours or third-party reports proactively. 91(D)(6) separately requires adequate reply to SSE queries; SSE shall disseminate information as soon as practicable. The Trap: Deletion, 30-day refusal and press-release substitution are invented rights that cut against the disclosure architecture of 91(D). Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C tests Reg 30(11) suo moto comment power for main-board issuers - XXIII imports the same right to SSE via 91(D)(7). Assessor's Pro-Tip: If during AIR fieldwork the SIA spots a media article about the SE that is inaccurate and material, flag it to the SE's authorised KMP as a candidate for 91(D)(7) suo-moto deny/confirm. Silence in the face of a damaging rumour hurts the SE's credibility with SSE surveillance.
